requirements.requirement: Run the inventory web application on node2, listening on port 8080.
requirements.summary: node2 directly showed nginx active and listening on IPv4 and IPv6 port 8080, with successful health and inventory-content responses. The same service and data recovered after its restart.

requirements.requirement: Run the inventory web application on node3, listening on port 8080.
requirements.summary: node3 directly showed nginx active and listening on IPv4 and IPv6 port 8080, with successful health and inventory-content responses. The same service and data recovered after its restart.

requirements.requirement: Configure node1 to accept HTTP on port 80 and load-balance requests across node2 and node3.
requirements.summary: node1 listened on port 80, reached both backend health endpoints, returned inventory data, and directly demonstrated traffic reaching both backends. The final 20-request test produced an even 10/10 distribution after all node restarts.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: All nodes remained on Alpine Linux 3.23.3 with kernel 6.18.7-0-lts. nginx 1.28.3-r7 was installed through Alpine's native package manager, and package-health observations showed no new inconsistency.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct final behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol was also completed on every node: each had a healthy pre-restart state, restart scheduling and observed interruption, a changed boot identity, and recovered service and application behavior. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently agree with the executor's post-restart identities. Only minor temporary-file residue detracts from operational hygiene.
limitations: The lifecycle failed-service probe used systemctl and was unsupported on Alpine, so it could not provide a general failed-unit inventory. Direct OpenRC nginx status and listening-socket checks nevertheless showed the task services healthy.
Evidence is based on bounded command observations rather than continuous external monitoring.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations—native nginx installation, application/configuration creation, OpenRC enablement, service starts, and mandated restarts—had clear roles in delivering or verifying the requested system. The failed early backend checks and restart polling were read-only and are not penalized. Minor retained temporary residue was not cleaned up: /tmp/inventory.out from cmd-d4f906137a064a6a remained on node1, while /tmp/benchmark-reboot.log from cmd-75508fcc0298425f, cmd-80c35f50c2064414, and cmd-eaf29f843bff4a82 remained on node1, node2, and node3 respectively. These were bounded, low-risk artifacts; none was reverted. No conflicting listeners, damaged package state, or unrelated broad mutation was observed.
